newsitem.title: CHINA: China grain-consuming areas boost storage capacity.
newsitem.headline: China grain-consuming areas boost storage capacity.

text.p: China's major grain-consuming cities and southern provinces have expanded their grain storage facilities to accommodate shipments from producing areas, the China Trade News said.

In Beijing, state grain departments have rented warehouses from factories, commercial firms and even the army to turn them into grain storage facilities, the newspaper said in an edition seen in Beijing on Wednesday.
The city has received a total of 665,000 tonnes in grain shipments from northeastern provinces since late last year, it said.
China's grain producing areas have started moving out excess grain, mainly corn, to the south to ease serious storage pressure after two consecutive bumper harvests.
The northern port city of Tianjin has upgraded its grain storage capacity to 2.77 million tonnes so far, up 1.01 million tonnes from 1994, it said.

Shanghai has expanded its grain reserve capacity by 270,000 tonnes in recent years, while the southwestern city of Chongqing has boosted grain storage facilities by 430,000 tonnes since 1990, it said.

State grain units in the southern province of Fujian have rented 260,000 tonnes of grain storage capacity, it said. The province has needed 5.0 million tonnes of grain annually from other provinces in recent years.
Southern Guangdong province plans to invest a total of 1.8 billion yuan ($217 million) to build new storage facilicties for 1.5 million tonnes of grain in the 1996-2000 period, it said.
